title: Parashurama's challenge
hook: Rama strings the bow, and then has to decide where the arrow goes
carry: leave me my power to move

segments.voice: Yesterday: Parashurama's challenge. An axe on his shoulder, Vishnu's bow in his hand, and a dare for a young prince. Did you take a breath before answering a test? Today Rama answers, and the first book of the Ramayana closes. Day five hundred thirteen.

The king has begged and been ignored. The whole wedding party stands frozen on the road, the brides in their carriages, the soldiers with their hands near their swords. Every eye is on one young man, just married, who has been told to string a god's bow and then fight a warrior who has made kings tremble. If you were writing this scene, you might reach for a duel. Valmiki doesn't. What Rama does next is quick and quiet, and it ends with nobody hurt.
screen: `THE ROAD STANDS FROZEN.` → `A DUEL? NO.` → `QUICK, QUIET, NOBODY HURT.`

segments.voice: Rama speaks politely and firmly. He has heard what Parashurama did to avenge his father, he says, and he respects it. But you've taken me for someone weak. Watch. He takes the bow out of the sage's hands, strings it, and fits an arrow. Then comes the surprise. You're a brahmin, Rama says, and you're related to my teacher Vishvamitra, so I won't loose this at you. But a drawn arrow can't go to waste. It will destroy one of two things: your power to move freely through the world, or the worlds of merit you've won by your austerities. You choose. The text says the gods gathered in the sky to watch. And the fire goes out of Parashurama. He answers simply. I gave the whole earth away to the sage Kashyapa, and promised not to stay on it at night. Leave me my power to move. Take the worlds I've won. Rama looses the arrow, and those worlds are gone. Then the older warrior says he knows who is standing in front of him: the undying Lord, the slayer of the demon Madhu. He walks around Rama with respect and leaves for the Mahendra mountain. Rama hands Vishnu's bow to Varuna, the god of the waters, for keeping. The road clears, and the family rides into Ayodhya to music and banners. Valmiki closes his first book gently. Bharata goes to visit his mother's family in the kingdom of Kekaya, and Shatrughna goes with him. Rama stays home, and he and Sita grow in love, the text says, each living in the other's heart. Remember that Bharata is far away. It matters very soon.
screen: `RAMA STRINGS THE BOW.` · `ONE ARROW, TWO CHOICES.` · `PARASHURAMA GIVES UP HIS WORLDS.` · `THE FIRST BOOK CLOSES AT HOME.` · then, large: `BHARATA IS FAR AWAY.`

segments.voice: Sit and let the body go still. Think of a time you won an argument, or could have. Now picture Rama on that road: the bow strung, the arrow ready, and a choice not to point it at the person in front of him. Breathe in, and feel the strength you actually have. Breathe out, and feel how much of it you don't need to use. Rest in the space between those two breaths. The bell holds the time.
Parashurama's challenge, answered. Rama strings Vishnu's bow, spares the sage, and takes only the worlds he had won by austerity.
Your line: leave me my power to move. Today, if you win a point, let it land softly; you don't have to aim it at anyone. Day five hundred thirteen.

howItsDone: In devotional readings this episode is heard as one avatar of Vishnu meeting the next, and the Bala Kanda as the happy prelude before the Ayodhya Kanda's exile.

match.prompt: the bow and the arrow — tap the pairs.
pairs: is given Vishnu's bow to keep

myth: Rama kills Parashurama on the road
he spares him as a brahmin and takes only the worlds he had won.
before leaving he names him the undying Lord, slayer of Madhu.
the first book ends with Bharata at home in Ayodhya
Bharata goes to Kekaya, with Shatrughna.

fork.setup: you're Rama, holding a strung bow and an arrow that can't go to waste. what do you aim at?
options: the worlds of merit the sage has won.
fork.reveal: Rama spares the man and lets him choose: his free movement or his merit-worlds. Parashurama gives up the worlds.

original.note: Sanskrit dhanus: bow. two great bows, Shiva's broken at Mithila and Vishnu's strung on the road, close the first book.

trapdoor: what you thought: Rama defeats Parashurama in a great battle.
what it means: there's no fight; Rama strings the bow and spares him.

what a scholar hears: some scholars treat the Bala Kanda as a later layer of the epic, and see scenes like this one, where an avatar meets an avatar, as part of how Rama's divinity was drawn into the story.
